claim: In experiment, 619-nm DNA-coated polystyrene spheres in a two-dimensional chamber -- particle A carrying strand S, particle B a mixture of S and its complement S*, the mixing ratio alpha being the fraction of S on B -- crystallise as square checkerboard at alpha = 0, as hexagonal stripe from alpha = 0.1 (coexisting with checkerboard up to alpha = 0.3) and as hexagonal honeycomb at alpha = 0.5; at alpha = 0.3 a crystal nucleates square and becomes hexagonal as it grows, while at alpha = 0 and 0.5 it keeps its first symmetry.

numbers.name: dna_strand_fraction
numbers.note: the mixing ratio at which the two-step pathway was followed.

validity_conditions: AN EXPERIMENT, NOT A MODEL RESULT. Suspension at about 1.0% volume fraction and about 1:1 A:B, squeezed between two plasma-cleaned coverslips; the temperature quenched to just above the melting temperature (half the particles unbound) and held about an hour; bright-field video and confocal imaging. At alpha = 0.4 the stripe pattern is gone, leaving small A clusters surrounded by B. The crystals' A:B ratio falls from 1:1 to about 1:2 as alpha rises although every sample started at 1:1. The authors read the checkerboard-stripe coexistence at alpha 0.1-0.2 as an unfinished transition within experimental time. The companion simulation entries (binary_2d_gcmc_*) reproduce the same sequence in a model with no hydrodynamics.
